newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanians protest over failed pyramid schemes.
newsitem.headline: Albanians protest over failed pyramid schemes.

text.p: Hundreds of Albanian investors demonstrated in the northern city of Shkoder on Thursday, calling for the government's resignation over the collapse of pyramid schemes.
The financial scandals have stirred opposition parties into trying to make political capital out of the anger among investors against the ruling right-wing Democratic Party.
Nearly a thousand protesters gathered in front of Shkoder city hall to vent their anger over the failure of schemes into which some had poured their life savings.
"The government should resign, we want our money," protesters shouted.
"The government should have warned us long ago and not now. So it's better that it stands aside and leaves us to resolve the problem," a 60-year-old man called Frrok said.
"Was this the reward of democracy for Shkoder?" he asked.
Albanian newspapers reported the arrest of some 60 officials of two of the pyramid schemes, Xhaferri and Populli, including their top managers.
Authorities have already ordered the seizure of 25.5 billion leks ($255 million) deposited by the two schemes in state-owned banks.

"I live with your concern but I think such problems should be resolved calmly," Shkoder mayor Bahri Borici, who had himself put money in the schemes, said while trying to calm down the noisy crowd in front of his office.
Thousands clashed with baton-wielding police in Tirana on Sunday in a demonstration over the schemes, the biggest of several protests around Albania over the past two weeks.
More than 50 people have been jailed or given big fines for taking part in Sunday's protest, described by the authorities as an illegal demonstration.
Foreign Minister Tritan Shehu said in Portugal on Wednesday that the government planned to push a law through parliament on Thursday to abolish the get-rich-quick schemes.
Pyramid schemes proliferated in Albania after the fall of communism in 1990, luring thousands into selling their homes, land and livestock with promises of big returns.
The rightist National Front Party said "the government should beg forgiveness from the public and resign".
The party said in a statement that the government of President Sali Berisha had lost the moral right to govern for failing to prevent the Albanian people from being robbed.
An association of Albanians who suffered political persecution under the former communist regime came out in support of the protests, and called for fresh elections and a new constitution.
The main opposition Socialist Party, heirs to the former communists, urged closer cooperation among the opposition and called for a peaceful protest on Sunday at Tirana's main soccer stadium.
"Politics should come out into the streets together with the people," an editorial in the Socialist daily Zeri i Popullit said. "Those who remain indifferent to this problem will be lost forever."
The ruling Democrats have dismissed suggestions that popular protests would threaten the government.
